tasks.title: Bootstrap cargo crate with pinned dependency stack
acceptance: `Cargo.toml` declares package name `todoist-tui`, edition 2021, a single binary target `todoist-tui`, and pins (exact major.minor) all of: ratatui, crossterm, tokio (rt-multi-thread + macros), reqwest with default-features=false and features ["json","rustls-tls"], rusqlite (bundled), serde+serde_json, keyring, uuid (v4), tracing + tracing-subscriber + tracing-appender, thiserror, anyhow, clap (derive), toml, directories (or dirs) for platform paths
No dependency enables OpenSSL: `cargo tree -i openssl-sys` reports no such package (command output pasted in PR)
`rust-toolchain.toml` pins a stable channel and includes components rustfmt and clippy
`src/main.rs` compiles as a placeholder entrypoint (prints nothing in library terms; may return Ok) and declares no modules yet
`cargo build` succeeds and `Cargo.lock` is committed
`.gitignore` ignores `/target`, and local artefacts; it does not ignore `Cargo.lock`
tasks.context: Greenfield repo: this is the first Rust file in the tree. Binary crate (not workspace). Keep module files out of this PR - later tasks add them. Requirement REQ-001 mandates HTTPS via rustls only. keyring pulls dbus/secret-service on Linux: confirm `cargo build` works and note any system packages needed in the PR description (CI job in T-008 verifies on a clean container).

tasks.title: Add rustfmt and clippy lint configuration
acceptance: `rustfmt.toml` exists with explicit edition and max_width settings; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes on the current tree

`Cargo.toml` gains a `[lints.rust]` / `[lints.clippy]` section denying at minimum `unwrap_used` and `expect_used` in non-test code (warn-level acceptable only if documented in the PR) plus `clippy::all` and `clippy::pedantic` at warn
`clippy.toml` sets project thresholds (e.g. `too-many-lines`, `cognitive-complexity-threshold`) used by the above lints
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0 on the current tree
tasks.context: Touches Cargo.toml again after T-001 - rebase on it, do not re-pin dependencies here. Lint strictness must still allow later epics to compile; prefer warn for pedantic, deny for the unwrap/expect pair.

tasks.title: Define typed error hierarchy in src/error.rs
acceptance: `src/error.rs` defines `AppError` (thiserror) with at least variants `Config(ConfigError)`, `Log(LogError)`, `NotImplemented(&'static str)` and a crate-wide `pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, AppError>`

`ConfigError` is a thiserror enum with variants carrying the config file `PathBuf` and, for parse failures, a line/column (e.g. `Parse { path: PathBuf, line: usize, column: usize, message: String }`), plus `Io { path, source }`
`Display` for every variant includes the offending file path; no variant interpolates a secret value
Unit test: `AppError::from(ConfigError::Parse{..})` renders a message containing the path and the line number
`src/main.rs` declares `mod error;` and still builds
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
tasks.context: Pure types, no IO. thiserror for library-style typed errors, anyhow only at the top of main. These variants are extended by later epics (ApiError, StoreError) - keep the enum non_exhaustive-friendly and the module free of domain logic.

tasks.title: Resolve platform config/state/data directories
acceptance: `paths::config_file()` returns `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/todoist-tui/config.toml` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set, else the platform default (`~/.config/todoist-tui/config.toml` on Linux, Application Support on macOS, AppData on Windows)
`paths::state_dir()` returns `$XDG_STATE_HOME/todoist-tui` when set, else the platform default; `paths::log_file()` is `<state_dir>/todoist-tui.log`
Directory creation helper `ensure_state_dir()` creates the state dir recursively and is idempotent (calling twice succeeds)
All path functions return `Result<PathBuf, ConfigError>` - no panics and no `unwrap` when the home dir cannot be determined
Unit tests set `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`XDG_STATE_HOME` to a tempdir and assert the exact resolved paths; a test asserts `ensure_state_dir` is idempotent
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
tasks.context: Use the `directories`/`dirs` crate pinned in T-001 for non-XDG platforms, but honour XDG env vars first on all platforms so tests can redirect them. Env-var mutation in tests is process-global: serialise those tests (e.g. a mutex or `serial_test`-style guard) and document the choice. Windows fallbacks are best-effort per NFR.

tasks.title: Load layered config from TOML with defaults and typed errors
acceptance: `Config` derives serde Deserialize with fields `sync_interval: Duration|u64 secs`, `theme: String`, `keymap: HashMap<String,String>`, `default_view: DefaultView` enum (`inbox|today|upcoming`), all `#[serde(default)]`
`Config::default()` yields `sync_interval == 60` seconds, `default_view == Inbox`, empty keymap overrides, and a named default theme
`Config::load()` with no config file present returns the defaults and does not create the file; unit test asserts `sync_interval == 60`
Unit test with a tempdir `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` containing `config.toml` with `sync_interval = 120` and `default_view = "today"` returns a `Config` with those values and defaults for untouched fields
Unit test: malformed TOML returns `Err(ConfigError::Parse)` containing the config file path and the 1-based line number of the error; the test asserts the process does not panic
Unit test: unknown key in config.toml is rejected OR ignored - behaviour is asserted explicitly and documented in a doc comment
Debug impl for `Config` is derived and contains no secret fields (config holds no secrets in this epic)
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
tasks.context: Depends on T-004 for `paths::config_file()`. Use the `toml` crate; map `toml::de::Error::span()`/line info into `ConfigError::Parse`. Keymap is a free-form string map here - EPIC-07 interprets it; do not validate key names yet.

tasks.title: Tracing to rotating state-dir log file with secret redaction
acceptance: `log::init(LogOptions)` installs a `tracing_subscriber` writing to a daily-rotating file appender under `paths::state_dir()`, returning a guard the caller must keep alive
In TUI mode (default) nothing is written to stdout or stderr by the subscriber; a non-TUI/`--verbose` mode may add a stderr layer, selected via `LogOptions`
Log level is read from `RUST_LOG` (`EnvFilter`) with a documented default of `info`
A `Secret<T>` (or `redact()` helper) type is provided whose `Display`/`Debug` render exactly `***` and which exposes the inner value only via an explicit `expose()` method
Unit test: a `Secret` wrapping the literal `tok_abc123` is logged at info level into a tempdir state dir; the written log file contains `***` and a grep for `tok_abc123` finds zero occurrences
Unit test: calling `init` writes the log file at `<state_dir>/todoist-tui.log*` and the state dir is created when missing
`src/main.rs` declares `mod log;` and builds; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
tasks.context: Depends on T-004 for state dir. Use `tracing-appender` rolling + `NonBlocking` (hold the `WorkerGuard` in main). Name the module `log` but avoid clashing with the `log` crate facade. The redaction helper is the seam EPIC-02 uses for the API token and EPIC-12's automated log scan test.

tasks.title: Clap CLI skeleton with not-implemented subcommand stubs
acceptance: `todoist-tui --help` lists subcommands `auth`, `logout`, `sync`, `add`, `today` with one-line descriptions
`add` accepts a single positional `<TEXT>` argument (quick-add text per REQ-001 D1); no parsing of that text happens in this task
`today` accepts a `--json` flag; `sync` and the rest take no extra args in this epic
Running with no subcommand selects the default TUI path, which currently prints `not implemented` to stderr and exits with code 1
Each subcommand stub returns `AppError::NotImplemented(<name>)`; `main` maps it to a `not implemented: <name>` stderr message and exit code 1 (no panic, no backtrace)
`main` initialises config (T-005) and logging (T-006) before dispatch, holding the log guard for the process lifetime; `--config <path>` global flag overrides the config file location
Test (trycmd/assert_cmd or a unit test on the clap `Command`) asserts the help output contains all five subcommand names and that `--version` prints the crate version
`cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean
tasks.context: clap derive. Keep stubs free of any network/DB/UI code - EPIC-02/03/06/11 fill them in. Verify the clap command tree with `Command::debug_assert()` in a unit test. The `add` positional exists only so EPIC-11 can attach behaviour without changing the CLI surface.

tasks.title: CI workflow running fmt, clippy and tests
acceptance: Workflow triggers on `push` and `pull_request` to the default branch
Job matrix covers `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest`; each job runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --all` and `cargo build --release`
Toolchain comes from `rust-toolchain.toml` (no separately hard-coded version) and cargo registry/target caching is enabled
A dedicated Linux job installs the minimal system packages required by `keyring` (libdbus/libsecret dev packages) and documents them in a comment, proving the build works on a bare container
Workflow is verified green once on a pushed branch (run link pasted in the PR); a deliberately mis-formatted file makes the fmt step fail (verified once, then reverted)
tasks.context: Mirrors the local commands recorded in CLAUDE.md by T-009. EPIC-12 later adds integration/perf gate jobs - keep job names stable and generic (fmt, clippy, test, build) so they can be extended.
